library_preparation_preflight.summary: The only failure is a Kotlin toolchain mismatch. The tests are compiled by Kotlin compiler 2.3.0 (from the `libs.plugins.kotlin.jvm` catalog alias), but kotlin-scripting-common:2.5.0-Beta1 ships 2.5.0 metadata, and compiler 2.3.0 reads only up to 2.4.0. The library itself needs no extra dependency, Docker image or environment setup.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: In the new 2.5.0-Beta1 test project, the Kotlin Gradle plugin must be at least as new as the library, or compileTestKotlin cannot read the 2.5.0-metadata classes. Do not use `alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.jvm)` here, because it resolves to the 2.3.x plugin the existing 2.3.21 project uses. Pin the plugin to 2.5.0-Beta1 explicitly, for example `id 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm' version '2.5.0-Beta1'`, or add a version-catalog entry used only by this project. Leave the 2.3.21 project untouched. Keep `kotlin-reflect` and `kotlin-stdlib` aligned to the same version as the library (`$libraryVersion`). If the Beta1 plugin does not resolve from Gradle Plugin Portal or Maven Central, a fallback is `kotlinOptions.freeCompilerArgs += '-Xskip-metadata-version-check'`. Do not rely on it unless the pin fails, since newer compilers may still choke on the metadata. Beta artifacts and the Kotlin toolchain also need to run under JDK 25.

The Kotlin 2.5.0-Beta1 compiler may not support JDK 25 as the jvmToolchain or jvmTarget.
Changing the plugin version in the shared version catalog would affect every other Kotlin test project, so keep the pin local to this project.
